title: ByteWolf Offboard Setpoint Contract v0.1
description: One continuously streamed velocity setpoint offered to the Offboard control boundary. Unlike an observation, this IS a command -- which is exactly why every field that decides whether it may be obeyed is mandatory and explicit. This contract carries no arm, mode, actuator or motor field, and never will: those are PX4's, not this boundary's. Acceptance is decided by brain/control/boundary.py against shared/config/x500v2/twin.yaml; a document that merely satisfies this schema has not been approved for flight. See docs/offboard-control-v0_1.md.

contract_version.description: Pins the meaning of every field below. A consumer that does not know this version must reject the setpoint rather than guess what it commands.

vehicle_id.description: The twin this setpoint commands; must match vehicle.id in twin.yaml. A setpoint meant for another vehicle is refused, not adapted.

stream_id.description: One continuous control session. Sequence numbers are only comparable within a stream, so a restarted producer must issue a new stream_id instead of reusing sequence numbers the boundary has already seen.

sequence.description: Strictly increasing within a stream. This is what makes a duplicated or reordered setpoint detectable: a network that delivers an old command late must not be able to reverse a newer one.

issued_at.description: RFC 3339, UTC, with an explicit offset. When the producer computed this command, never when it was sent or received: the age that decides expiry is measured from the instant the decision was made, so a slow link cannot hide behind a fresh transmit time.

ttl_s.description: How long this setpoint may be acted on after issued_at. A producer may ask for less than the vehicle's configured maximum; asking for more is refused rather than clamped, because a producer that misunderstands its own freshness budget is not one to negotiate with.

frame.description: The coordinate frame the velocity is expressed in, stated rather than assumed. 'local_ned': north/east/down relative to the local origin. 'body_frd': forward/right/down relative to the airframe. The boundary accepts exactly the frame twin.yaml configures and rejects the other -- a frame mismatch is a sign error in a movement command, which is not something to infer.

kind.description: v0.1 carries velocity setpoints only. Trajectory setpoints are deliberately absent rather than declared-but-unimplemented: a contract that names a capability the boundary cannot validate would invite a producer to send one.

validity.description: What the producer knows about its own command. 'invalid' means the producer computed something it does not trust; the boundary rejects it. There is no 'missing': a command that does not exist is simply not sent, and silence is the watchdog's business.

velocity.description: The commanded velocity, interpreted in the declared frame. Every component is mandatory: an omitted axis would have to default to something, and a silent zero is a command in its own right.

x_m_s.description: North in local_ned, forward in body_frd. Metres per second.

y_m_s.description: East in local_ned, right in body_frd. Metres per second.

z_m_s.description: Down in both frames, positive downward, matching PX4's convention rather than inverting it here where the sign would be easy to lose. Metres per second.

yaw_rate_deg_s.description: Positive clockwise seen from above. Degrees per second.

uncertainty_m_s.description: The producer's own estimate of how wrong this velocity could be. Optional, but a producer that can estimate it and stays silent gets no benefit of the doubt: the boundary applies its limit only when the field is present, so omitting it is a claim of confidence.
